rawFindings.title: Incorrect property reading logic in v1 readObject - dropped label update causes infinite loop
rawFindings.explanation: In the patched code, the prior logic reading a property and then updating the label to check for the ending label 'z' is replaced with an unconditional read of the property without updating the label, which will cause the loop to never observe label 'z', causing infinite loop or incorrect parsing.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original logic that reads a key, then a value, then updates the label for termination check. For example: key = this.read(withType); value = this.read(withType); label = this.byteBuffer.getChar(); if (!/^this$\d+$/.test(key)) { result.$[key] = value; }

rawFindings.title: Incorrect property reading logic in v2 readObject - dropped loop control update causes infinite loop
rawFindings.explanation: The patch removes the conditional check and label update inside the object property reading loop, causing the loop to lose the termination condition and thus likely fail or loop infinitely.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original code inside the loop that reads the value, checks the property name, assigns if appropriate, and then moves to the next field.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect object property reading in v1 decoder readObject
rawFindings.explanation: In the function readObject for the v1 decoder, the code was changed to always assign to result.$[key] using this.read(withType). This removes the previous check which filtered out keys matching /^this\$\d+$/, and incorrectly changes the order of reading label and value. rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the order of reading value and label as in original code to correctly consume the stream. Also, reinstate the check to exclude keys matching /^this\$\d+$/, as these are internal fields in Java and should not be included in the decoded object's public properties.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect object property reading in v2 decoder readObject
rawFindings.explanation: In the v2 decoder's readObject function, similarly to v1, the patch changed the reading of object fields to always assign result.$[name] = this.read(withType). This removes the check to exclude fields named /^this\$\d+$/, which are internal Java fields and are intended to be skipped. Ignoring this may cause unintended inclusion of private/internal fields and lead to faulty decoded objects.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the conditional check to exclude keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ from being added as object properties, as in the original code, to avoid exposing internal fields improperly.
